sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r12/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 42; Internal Quality Checks row 42 note 'Mukesh - we need to monitor this one.'), read in memory with openpyxl read_only
evidence: STATIC STRUCTURE (supports monotonicity): tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff against rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml empty): gates render/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floors functional=0.05. tests/tools/score.py and tests/test.sh are identical to the template (diff empty). score.py:41-48: reward = weighted mean of positive weights only when gates_passed and functional>0.05, else 0.0; all weights positive, so an app that is >= another on every dimension never scores lower (Pareto-monotone). Function carries 0.6 > craft 0.4, so no craft-over-function inversion of the kind quality-checks.md#42 names. Per-criterion weights (parsed with tomllib): functional 44 binary criteria sum 59.5 (min share 0.84%), polish 5 binary sum 12, visual 5 likert(points=5) sum 6 equal 1.2 each; gates 1 binary each, all_pass. No negative or zero weights. GATES vs STRONGER APP: gates/render/judge.toml:22-24 (wrong password stays signed out; correct Recruiter sign-in shows a workspace) and gates/constraints/judge.toml:46-48 (Recruiter opens job + adds candidate via UI; Observer in an independent context sees exactly one card in Applied) demand only behaviour required by public hireops_rules.md sec.1-2 and sec.3 (Observer reads the board, cards start in Applied, interview places 1-50). I found no gate a better conforming app could fail while a weaker one passes. SHELL FARMING BLOCKED: polish/prompt.md and visual/prompt.md both repeat the same shared-storage browser gate and give binary0 / Likert1 (normalised 0) to a static or non-persisting shell, so a pretty dead app cannot collect the 0.4 craft mass; plus the functional floor. NEGATIVES HAVE CONTROLS (prevents dead features out-scoring working ones): e.g. functional hro_mgr_early_refused (judge.toml:155 'their late-stage moves are the control'), hro_activity_refusals (:281 'successful actions' lines are the control'), hro_undo_once (:263), hro_candidate_private (:398 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), hro_candidate_no_staff (:182), hro_anonymous (:191 'A signed-in success of each is the control'); polish hro_pol_live_board/live_thread score 0 when no update arrives (:71,:80), hro_pol_failed_send needs a successful resend (:98). Functional prompt: 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'. Status codes graded in hro_refusal_status/hro_anonymous (401/403/404/409) are public in hireops_rules.md:21-23,:77-78, so a conforming app is not ranked below a nonconforming one there. RESIDUAL RANKING RISKS (latent, unmeasured): (1) Budget/ordering inversion: functional is one batched judge (judge.toml timeout=9000) walking 44 criteria in protocol order; evaluator/budget exhaustion converts unobserved rows to 0 ('NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation', functional/polish/visual prompts). A better app whose controls succeed forces the judge deeper through each protocol and may exhaust budget before later rows, while a worse app fast-fails early protocols and reaches later rows, so a better app could outscore lower under budget pressure. (2) Craft trade-off: with the template floor 0.05, an app at ~0.06 functional with top polish/visual (~0.436 if it somehow passed live-update polish rows; realistically ~0.236 with visual only) can beat a ~30%-functional app with poor visuals (0.6*0.30+0.2*0.25=0.23). This is the mandated template shaping (skill 'Delivery profile') not a task defect, and polish rows depend on live features so the realistic gap is small. (3) Double counting: live board/thread failures cost both functional hro_live_board (2.5/59.5) and polish live rows (6/12); this amplifies but does not invert ranking. MEASUREMENT GAP: qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r12/raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' I verified all 6 indexed artifact hashes and all 12 matching_source_files hashes against the frozen task (all match); they are scripted golden observations only, not reward-ordering runs. No mutated weak-app vs golden reward comparison exists, so ranking monotonicity of the actual judge (z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx via claude-code) is not exercised. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record before clearance; it is missing. Static design shows no inversion defect, but per skill 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass'.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated Fail. Plausible unmeasured inversion: under the single 9000 s batched functional judge, a stronger app whose positive controls all succeed may exhaust the judge budget before the later protocols (T/U/K/D, worth ~40% of functional weight), which then score 0 as NOT EXERCISED, while a weaker app that fast-fails the board protocols leaves budget to pass those later rows. Conforming-alternative check: no gate or criterion found that penalises a conforming app relative to a nonconforming one.
suggested_fix: Produce the hash-bound reward-ordering record the policy requires: run the full configured verifier on the golden and on graded mutants (e.g. no live updates; no undo; no candidate privacy; dead shell with good styling) and confirm reward(golden) > reward(each mutant) and that no row is lost to budget exhaustion on the golden.
